title: Family planning — WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (draft)
summary: WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) framework for contraceptive method selection. The category system (1-4) is the universal decision framework; the full condition-by-method tables are referenced (not reproduced) and authored as structured rules during clinical review. DRAFT — clinician verification required before approval.

categories.meaning: No restriction on use of the method.
Advantages generally outweigh theoretical or proven risks.
Theoretical or proven risks usually outweigh advantages — method not usually recommended unless other methods unavailable/unacceptable.
Unacceptable health risk — method should not be used.

principles: Apply MEC categories to the individual's conditions to determine safe method options.
Support informed choice; counsel on effectiveness, dual protection (STI/HIV), and side effects.
Quick-start eligible methods when reasonably certain not pregnant.
redFlags: Category 4 conditions for a requested method (e.g. combined hormonal contraception with current breast cancer, <6 weeks postpartum breastfeeding for some methods, severe uncontrolled hypertension) — select an alternative.
nationalOverlayNotes: Per-country overlays should map the available method mix and any national MEC adaptations.

references.label: WHO Medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use, 5th edition
